name: What causes drafts in sliding doors?

mainEntity.name: What causes drafts in sliding doors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Drafts in sliding doors are commonly caused by worn-out weatherstripping, damaged door seals, or gaps in the door frame. Over time, materials can degrade due to exposure to elements, leading to air leaks. Misaligned doors or issues with the rollers can also prevent the door from closing properly, creating spaces for drafts to enter. Addressing these issues can significantly improve energy efficiency and comfort.
acceptedAnswer.description: Drafts are usually caused by worn weatherstripping, damaged seals, or misaligned doors, allowing air to leak through gaps.
